propositions: materialize_tickets writes every blob in the ticket tree fresh on every attested gate resolution without reusing content from adjacent entries differing by single files, producing ~620 MiB copies on a cache key advancing every ~26 seconds with effectively zero reuse

The snapshot store's content-addressed `tickets-<sha>` entries lack hardlinking or delta materialization against prior entries, causing 10^5x write amplification (one-file delta produces full 620 MiB copy) and linear byte growth with no reclaim

A single attested gate resolution under five concurrent agents materializes 620 MiB across 69,984 blobs, and this scales multiplicatively with concurrency, contributing to multi-agent host saturation measured at sustained load average 12+ with resource starvation

ADR 0005's design invariant that immutable SHAs are perfect cache keys assumes key reuse, which the tickets-branch tip key lacks because it advances ~26 seconds per commit; this breaks the bounded reclaimable cache contract

The fix employs hardlinking and delta materialization: pick the newest published `tickets-<sha2>` entry reachable in the clone, hardlink shared paths, and materialize only the paths that differ via git checkout-index, with git ls-tree and git show oracles verifying content integrity

Snapshot store byte accounting must track exclusive_size (st_nlink==1 files, the bytes added at populate and freed at evict) separately from entry_size (plain st_size for reporting) and distinct_bytes (inode deduplication ground truth) to avoid crediting bytes still on disk in the free-space watermark loop
